title: Impose an eight-page saddle-stitched booklet so the pages read in order once folded
instruction: Impose the eight pages on the four boards for a saddle-stitched booklet.
context: A saddle-stitched booklet is made from sheets printed on both sides, folded, nested and stitched through the fold. Pages that follow each other in reading order are therefore not side by side on the sheet: in an eight-page booklet of two sheets, page 8 sits beside page 1 and page 2 beside page 7. Working this out, called imposition, is a core prepress job, and a mistake means the whole print run comes out in the wrong order. Here the eight pages start scrambled and four boards stand for the four printed faces. Laying them out in reading order earns nothing. The robot has to work out where each page lands after folding, including which pages belong to the same sheet, with no diagram or numbering on the boards to help. The instruction names the binding only; it does not give the layout. Done by: prepress technicians and print finishers.
setup: A brown bench surface (46 x 84 cm) covers the table. Four blue painted boards (7 cm deep, 20 cm wide, 4 mm thick), centred 45.5 cm out and 13 cm left, 35 cm out and 13 cm left, 45.5 cm out and 13 cm right, 35 cm out and 13 cm right. The two boards on the same side of the table are the two faces of one sheet. Each board has two pale 5.6 cm square page positions, centred 4.5 cm left and right of its centre, with a dark fold line between them and a dark head bar along its far edge marking the top of the page. Eight white wooden page blocks (5 cm cube, 100 g), each with its page number in black on top, top of the number away from the arms, stand in a row 22 cm out: 7 at 30 cm left, 1 at 21.5 left, 5 at 13 left, 2 at 4.5 left, 3 at 4.5 right, 8 at 13 right, 6 at 21.5 right, 4 at 30 right. The booklet is bound on the left and read left to right. Left and right are as seen from the arms. Also beyond the bench: a stack of paper reams, two ink tins and a proof sheet.
scoring: A page counts when its block stands upright (tilted less than 10 degrees), at rest on the board, with its centre within 2.5 cm of a position's centre. A sheet scores only when all four of its positions are filled and it holds pages 1, 2, 7 and 8 or pages 3, 4, 5 and 6. On such a sheet, each board earns 0.125 if its two pages add up to nine and a further 0.125 if the even page is on the left. Maximum 1.0. Any other layout of a sheet scores 0 for that sheet. Scored at the end.
reset_notes: Stand the eight blocks back in their row in the listed order; nothing is consumed.
fidelity: Rigid wooden blocks stand for pages, and boards for the faces of each sheet; nothing is printed or folded. Real imposition is done with plates or software, usually for many more pages. The scorer checks which page is in which position, as a prepress checker would with a folding dummy.
